body: Mauboussin paradox of skill: as skill rises, luck matters more. Proving 2% alpha needs ~16–64 years of data. Only 3 ten-year beat-the-market streaks among 5,593 funds.
title: Luck vs skill takes decades to separate

body: Sequence of leadership: 1991-92 operator stocks (ACC) and 1993-94 new issues -> 1998-2000 ICE/tech (K-10, Zee, HFCL) -> 2003-08 realty, infra, power, capital goods, metals -> 2009-2019 consumer staples/discretionary, private banks, NBFCs, pharma/IT 'quality' (the 2019-20 quality-premium peak) -> 2020-24 PSUs, defence, railways, capital goods, manufacturing, small caps -> 2025-26 large financials and autos leading the recovery with FPI buying in Nov 2026. After each bull, its leaders took years to regain their highs or never did: K-10 stocks averaged -51.7% in the year to Feb 2002 and many never recovered; the capital goods index needed ~2007-2021; realty fell ~90% in 2008 and Nifty Realty is still well below its 2008 high (unverified current level); PSU/railway names were -46-59% from July 2024 peaks by 2025. Why: the leading sector attracts the most capital (IPOs, capacity, leverage), so supply catches up and multiples peak there; the next leaders are usually the sectors starved of capital in the prior boom (capital-cycle logic). Implication: after a crash, screen the previous cycle's laggards with improving supply discipline, and be most skeptical of the last cycle's heroes, however good the story.
title: Indian bull-market leaders rarely lead the next cycle
